# Runix

> Runix builds tools that make AI effortless to use. Its flagship, Runix Router,
> is an LLM router: one OpenAI-compatible API in front of many model providers,
> with routing, automatic failover, central key custody, per-key quotas and
> per-request cost attribution. Operated by Runix AI Inc, a company incorporated
> in Wyoming, United States. The service is in early access — keys are issued on
> request rather than through self-serve signup.

## Products

Products at different stages. The statuses below are literal.

- **Runix Router** — *status: early access, running traffic today.* One OpenAI-compatible
  endpoint across many providers, positioned on security, compliance and performance:
  central key custody, per-key limits and quotas, request-level audit trail, contracts and
  written data terms, automatic failover between providers with streaming preserved, and
  routing by cost, health and configuration. Hosted API, billed on usage.
  https://runixcloud.io/router
- **Runix Pipeline** — *status: in development with design partners.* Managed data
  preparation for AI: ingestion, cleaning, three tiers of deduplication, schema-validated
  LLM extraction, PII masking that fails closed, and a quality report with every delivery.
  Scoped and priced per project or volume. https://runixcloud.io/pipeline
- **Runix Code** — *status: in development, waitlist open.* An AI coding agent being built
  for teams: codebase-aware completion and chat, agentic multi-file tasks that land as
  reviewable diffs, and team controls (seats, usage attribution, model routing policies,
  written data terms). Not generally available. https://runixcloud.io/code
- **Runix Comic** — *status: in development, waitlist open.* An end-to-end AI studio for
  comic dramas being built to cover pre-production (scripts, consistent characters,
  storyboards), production (styled panels, motion, voice-over, subtitles) and publishing
  (export, multi-platform distribution, promotional assets). Not generally available.
  https://runixcloud.io/comic

## Facts a buyer usually asks for

- Legal entity: Runix AI Inc, Wyoming, United States.
- Contracting: MSA and DPA on request, reviewed per engagement; an order form takes
  precedence over the standard Terms.
- Billing: USD, usage-based (per token or per request, by model), itemised statements,
  prepaid draw-down or invoiced. There is no published rate card; quotes are per workload.
- Data handling: customer prompt and response content is not used to train models and is
  not sold. Operational metadata (usage counts, latency, error codes) is kept to run
  billing, reliability and support. Details in the Privacy Policy and Security page.
- Certifications: none are claimed. Runix does not assert SOC 2, ISO 27001 or PCI status.
- Support: replies within one business day, contact@runixcloud.io.

## Writing

All 23 posts, newest first. Descriptions are the pages' own.

- [How to tell whether a model change made things worse](https://runixcloud.io/blog/did-the-model-change-make-it-worse) — Output varies run to run, so a quality regression does not announce itself. Four signals that move before anyone files a ticket.
- [How long should an LLM request be allowed to take?](https://runixcloud.io/blog/how-long-should-an-llm-request-wait) — Standard HTTP timeout advice is wrong for model traffic. Which timeout to set, where each one belongs, and why stacked timeouts cause the outage.
- [Migrating to a gateway without a maintenance window](https://runixcloud.io/blog/migrating-to-an-llm-gateway-without-downtime) — Shadow, then a percentage, then a cutover you can reverse in one config change — and the three things about LLM traffic the usual playbook does not cover.
- [Your model id has an expiry date](https://runixcloud.io/blog/model-deprecation-without-a-redeploy) — Providers retire model versions on a published schedule. If the id is a string literal in your code, their calendar is your deploy calendar.
- ["OpenAI-compatible" is a surface, not a contract](https://runixcloud.io/blog/what-openai-compatible-actually-means) — Compatibility claims cover the endpoint shape, rarely the details that break you: ignored parameters, missing usage, streaming that ends wrong. How to test one.
- [Comic Drama vs Webtoon vs Motion Comic, Explained](https://runixcloud.io/blog/comic-drama-vs-webtoon-vs-motion-comic) — Three overlapping formats for drawn stories: how webtoons, motion comics and comic dramas differ in production, distribution and audience — and which to make.
- [How to Make a Comic Drama with AI: Script to Screen](https://runixcloud.io/blog/how-to-make-a-comic-drama-with-ai) — The full AI comic drama production line: script and characters, storyboards, styled panels, motion, voice and publishing — and where tools still fall short.
- [LLM Router vs LLM Gateway: What's the Difference?](https://runixcloud.io/blog/llm-router-vs-llm-gateway) — The two names describe overlapping tools. What routing and gateway features actually do, when the difference matters, and how to choose on capabilities.
- [12 Data Questions to Ask an AI Vendor](https://runixcloud.io/blog/ai-vendor-data-questions) — The data-handling questions that decide an AI procurement review, what a good answer sounds like, and which vague replies should stop the process.
- [Build or Buy an LLM Gateway: An Honest Comparison](https://runixcloud.io/blog/build-vs-buy-llm-gateway) — The first version of a gateway is a weekend. The parts that take a year are retry budgets, streaming failover, cost accounting and being on call for all of it.
- [LLM Provider Keys: Scope, Rotation and Blast Radius](https://runixcloud.io/blog/llm-api-key-management) — Provider keys spread through repos, CI and notebooks. How to scope and rotate them, and why a compromised LLM key is a billing incident as well as a data one.
- [Per-Team LLM Cost Attribution That Survives Audit](https://runixcloud.io/blog/llm-cost-attribution) — Provider invoices arrive as one number. How to attach cost to a team, feature and request at call time, and why reconstructing it later never works.
- [What to Log for LLM Traffic, and What Not To](https://runixcloud.io/blog/llm-observability) — Status codes and latency miss the failures that matter for LLM traffic. The signals worth recording, the fields to redact, and the alerts worth waking up for.
- [Surviving LLM Rate Limits: 429s, Budgets and Queues](https://runixcloud.io/blog/llm-rate-limits) — Why provider rate limits bite in bursts, how RPM, TPM and concurrency interact, and the queueing and backoff patterns that keep throughput stable under 429s.
- [OpenRouter Alternatives: A Buyer's Checklist](https://runixcloud.io/blog/openrouter-alternatives) — Evaluating LLM gateways beyond routing: the contract, data, failover and cost-attribution questions that decide whether a gateway survives procurement.
- [Prompt Caching: When It Pays and When It Bites](https://runixcloud.io/blog/prompt-caching-explained) — How provider-side prompt caching works, the prefix rule that decides whether you get hits, and the cases where caching quietly changes behaviour.
- [Streaming LLM Responses Without Breaking Failover](https://runixcloud.io/blog/streaming-llm-failover) — Once tokens have reached the user, failover stops being free. Mid-stream failure modes, what a proxy must preserve, and how to degrade without duplicating text.
- [What Is an LLM Gateway? A Plain Definition](https://runixcloud.io/blog/what-is-an-llm-gateway) — An LLM gateway is a control plane between your application and model providers. What it does, what it does not do, and when a team actually needs one.
- [LLM Cost Control: Tokens, Caching and Budgets](https://runixcloud.io/blog/llm-cost-control) — Token pricing asymmetry, prompt caching, model routing, budgets and kill switches — and the waste patterns that quietly inflate an LLM bill.
- [Building AI Data Pipelines: Raw to Model-Ready](https://runixcloud.io/blog/ai-data-pipelines) — A stage-by-stage guide to AI data pipelines: ingestion, cleaning, deduplication, LLM-powered extraction, PII masking and quality scoring.
- [Model Failover for Production LLM Traffic](https://runixcloud.io/blog/model-failover) — Keeping LLM-backed products up when providers degrade: failure taxonomy, retry budgets, circuit breakers, failover trade-offs and degradation tiers.
- [Choosing an LLM Gateway: 7 Things That Matter](https://runixcloud.io/blog/llm-gateway-guide) — How to evaluate an LLM gateway: API compatibility, failover behaviour, rate limits, cost tracking, observability, security and operational burden.
- [Introducing Runix](https://runixcloud.io/blog/introducing-runix) — Why we are building an OpenAI-compatible LLM gateway, managed data pipelines and ready-to-deploy solutions — and what comes next.
